Whereas the City of Argyle is authorized to issue a license for the sale of alcoholic beverages, pursuant to O.C.G.A. Section 3-3-2, and. Whereas ascertainable standards must be set forth as provided by said law; Therefore, the following requirements are established: 1) The manufacturing, distributing, and selling by wholesale or retail of alcoholic beverages shall not be conducted in the City of Argyle, Georgia without a license from the City of Argyle. 2) Applications for a license shall be made to the City of Argyle Council. 3) All decisions of the City of Argyle Council approving, denying, suspending, or revoking any license shall be in writing with the reasons therefore stated and shall be mailed or delivered to the applicant. 4) No licensee shall permit his place of business to be open for the sale of malt or alcoholic beverages on Sunday, election days, during voting hours, during the twenty-four (24) hour period of Christmas, or any other day or times during or upon which the sale of malt or alcoholic beverages is prohibited by law. 5) No licensee shall permit drinking on the premises. A sign stating “No drinking on the Premises” should be placed at the licensee's place of business. This sign should be visible to all customers. 6) Upon timely application, any person aggrieved by the decision of the City of Argyle regarding a license shall be afforded a hearing with an opportunity to present evidence and cross exam opposing witnesses. The person shall request a hearing in writing within thirty (30) days of the decision of the City of Argyle. 7) As a prerequisite to the issuance of any license, the applicant shall furnish a complete set of fingerprints to be forwarded to the Georgia Bureau of Investigation in accordance with O.C.G.A. Section 3-3-2. 8) Prior to action upon any application, a notice shall be published in the Clinch County News for at least ten (10) days prior to the next regular or call meeting at which the applicant is to be considered. Such notice shall contain the name of the applicant and the location of the proposed business. 9) In passing upon an application for a license, the City of Argyle shall be guided by the following standards: a) The proximity of other establishments selling malt or alcoholic beverages to the proposed location. b) The character of the neighborhood immediately adjacent to the proposed location. c) The proximity of churches, schools, day care facilities, and playgrounds to the proposed location. d) Whether the proposed location has adequate off street parking facilities or other parking available for the patrons.

Page 2 of 2 e) Whether the location would tend to increase and promote traffic congestion and resulting hazards therefrom. f) The feelings and attitudes of the citizens residing in the area adjacent to the proposed location. g) The information set forth in the application. h) Whether any malt or alcoholic beverage license previously issued for such location was revoked for cause by the City of Argyle Council. i) Whether the applicant has ever sold malt or alcoholic beverages illegally in the municipality. 10) The sale of malt or alcoholic beverages within 100 yards of a school, church, playground or day care facility is prohibited. 11) A license issued under the provisions of this section shall permit the sale or manufacture of malt beverages only on the premises described in the application. 12) All premises used for the sale or manufacture of malt or alcoholic beverages shall be kept in a safe and sanitary condition as required by the ordinances of the city and the laws of this state. 13) Any ordinance or resolutions previously adopted by the City of Argyle in conflict with this ordinance are hereby repealed. 14) This ordinance shall take effect immediately upon passage by the City of Argyle Council.
